title: BLOCKFALL - a game currently being worked on with Astra and Opus.
author: WASD_armory
selftext:
some backstory - as a kid I always had a love for game design, had spent time learning different coding languages, and had been sure that was what I was going to do as a career. Unfortunately, things changed and I ended up moving in a different way, (where i ended up I love equally as much) and have since forgotten all I knew. but with the rise of ai coding models it’s given me a chance to enjoy the same passion I’ve had since I was a child. 

It’s been an awesome time getting the chance to create again. my game has mainly just been a fun chance to play something with my family and tune it to what I feel is the most fun. 

It’s had its page on steam for a week now, with less traffic than expected, but it’s cool nonetheless to see that other people have seen it. 

The game is a roguelite PvP shooter in a fully destructible world, with abilities, guns, modifications, and tools that you roll for between rounds to gain an advantage on your friends. It’s still in the early stages of development and could use some polish, I’ve been working for around 3 weeks on this, I’d say 7-10 hours a day. 

At the time of writing, there is:  
9 weapons   
60 mods   
8 abilities   
8 tools

I’d love some input or thoughts on this as someone who has been silently creating for awhile but unfamiliar with the space. As of now, I’ve had no input outside of my friends and family who are all forced to tell me it’s great regardless of what they think. 

If any of you guys want to check out the full page on steam, Here’s the link [BLOCKFALL STEAM PAGE](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4729140/BLOCKFALL/)

comments.author: m4bwav
comments.body:
9 weapons and 60 mods in three weeks is a lot of content, and a fully destructible PvP arena is an ambitious thing to take on right out of the gate. Nice to see someone come back to making games this way.

A few things I'm curious about: what engine are you on, and how did you handle the destruction, voxels/chunks or something custom? Syncing it over the network for PvP seems like the hard part. How do you split the work between Astra and Opus, does one plan and the other build? And where are the art and sound coming from?

replies.author: WASD_armory
replies.body:
Thanks! I’m using Unreal Engine 5. The destruction system is voxel/chunk based. Each voxel has a health value based on its material, and weapons deal environmental damage separately from normal player damage.

Networking is running through Steam. Keeping voxel destruction synchronized between the host and clients has definitely been the most challenging part. It usually runs without issues now, but very large amounts of destruction happening at once can still cause problems, so that’s something I’m continuing to work on.

I initially built the game almost entirely using Astra. When Opus 5.5 released I started experimenting with it too, and so far I’ve found it considerably more efficient usage-wise for some tasks. I use both pretty interchangeably depending on what I’m working on.

the art has been made in Blender, as well as  model-written Python scripts when I need relatively simple models or repetitive modeling work. Audio has mostly come from commercially usable assets on Pixabay and Freesound.
